title: Protected corners and a trichotomy for Han's conjecture
summary: Han's conjecture predicts that a finite-dimensional algebra with eventually vanishing Hochschild homology has finite global dimension. In the tau-Hochschild framework of Cibils, Lanzilotta, Marcos and Solotar, it splits into persistence (Gap A) and survival (Gap B), and a Gap-A failure is already a counterexample. We prove a protected corner theorem bounding Ext at a surviving vertex, settling the Liu-Morin extension conjecture beyond the monomial and special biserial cases.
